framework.notes:
- **Texture packs.** The framework can now re-skin the game: replacement art
  for any sprite or sheet, and replacement wording for any of the game's
  1229 lines of text, in any of its 11 languages. You build one in the mod
  manager's new **Texture packs** tab; the framework applies it while the game
  runs. Nothing in your install is rewritten, which is the whole point - a
  Steam update can't wipe it, turning it off is instant, and there is no
  backup to restore. Packs are zips you can hand to anyone, and they can be
  published to the registry like modpacks.
  The console (F10) grew `texturepack` to show what the active pack replaced,
  `texturepack list` for every override in it, and `texturepack reapply` to
  put it back on without restarting.
- Mods still win over texture packs: a mod that ships its own art is loaded
  first, so a re-skin can never break a mod's UI.

manager.notes:
- **Every mod, modpack and texture pack now has its own page** - in the app
  and on the website. In the app, click any card for the whole story:
  description, the gambits at full size, release notes, downloads, license,
  provenance. On the web, the same page lives at
  `bentrd.github.io/GambonanzaMods/mod/<id>/` with an **Open in Mod Manager**
  button that jumps straight to it in the app.
- **Deep links.** The app registers the `gmm://` scheme: `gmm://mod/<id>`,
  `gmm://modpack/<id>` and `gmm://texturepack/<id>` open the matching page,
  whether the app is already running or not. Links carry a registry id and
  nothing else - never a URL or a file - so a malicious link can name a page
  but can't smuggle anything onto your machine, and nothing installs without
  the same confirmation as always. A **Copy link** button on every page hands
  you the website URL, which is the one to paste in Discord (Discord doesn't
  linkify `gmm://`, and friends without the app land on a download button
  instead of nothing).
- **The Play button no longer does nothing on Linux.** It hands the launch to
  Steam as before, but if the desktop has no handler for `steam://` - common on
  Linux, and the case with a Flatpak Steam - the manager starts the game's own
  executable instead and says so. When Steam refuses the handoff outright, that
  now shows up as an error on the button rather than silence.
- Fixed a bogus "could not fetch ... redirect with no destination" warning in
  the activity log. The registry index is fetched with the cached tag attached,
  and the "nothing changed since last time" reply was being mistaken for a
  broken redirect - so every cached refresh logged a failure it had not had.

mods.name: 'Point A' Manager
mods.author: Agent15
mods.summary: Library that remembers the tile each piece moved from, for other mods to build on.
mods.description: Not much to see on its own - install it because another mod asked for it. The game only remembers where a piece landed; this library tracks where it came from (for both player and enemy moves) and offers a helper to compute the distance and direction of the last move. Powers gambits like Recursion's and Sniper's.

mods.name: Better Collection
mods.author: Ben
mods.summary: Makes the gambit collection screen run smoothly.
mods.description:
The collection screen was drawing every card, button and arrow over itself up to 1250 times to fake a thick outline - the page arrows alone rebuilt as 7,500 shapes each, every time anything moved. This draws them twice instead: same look, a fraction of the cost. The run-info screen you open mid-run is built from the same pieces and gets the same treatment.

Prefer the chunkier outlines? Type 'collection outlines 4' in the console (F10) to put them back.

mods.name: Fall Guy
mods.author: Ben
mods.summary: Pieces about to fall are saved to the nearest free square, or the stash.
mods.description:
An Epic gambit for 8 coins. When the crumble takes a tile out from under one of your pieces, the piece does not die: it hops to the nearest intact empty square. If the whole board is out of squares it is dropped into your stash instead, ready to be placed again. Only when the stash is full too does the fall play out as vanilla wrote it.

Every fall is covered - there is no per-game limit. The buy-back graveyard is kept honest: a saved piece's booking is rolled back so a rescue is never also a free graveyard copy.

gambits.name: Fall Guy's Gambit
gambits.description: Pieces about to <color=§>FALL</color> are saved to the nearest free square, or the stash.

mods.name: Impatient Gambit
mods.author: Ben
mods.summary: Skip every stage straight to its boss, and earn 4x gold.
mods.description:
A Legendary gambit for 10 coins. Buy it and the next game is your current stage's boss; every stage after that goes straight to its own boss too, so a run collapses from 25 games to 5. All gold earned is multiplied by 4 to keep that survivable - five payouts instead of twenty-five - and the win screen gains a fourth breakdown row showing the bonus.

The run's opening game is never skipped: vanilla never treats it as a boss fight either.
